searchText: Hello. Am I right that I can practically do it the same way (cut heavy files and paste it in HDD -> symlink them) in geth (or any other execution implementations)? In geth you can use `--ancients` to put the chain history on an hdd (no need to symlink stuff) but first off I have to wait until fully synced and only **then** play around with files? Or I can just wait 10 mins or something where chain history files will be created -> stop geth daemon -> apply "--ancients" and then geth will start puts heavy files on the hdd? Its best to do it before you even start syncing Otherwise you need to manually move the files around thanks a lot.
